question.problem: Expressed as a fraction in its simplest form, $\frac{2}{3}+(-\frac{4}{9})=${{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
First, we drop the parentheses and the addition sign, which gives 

$$
\frac{2}{3}+(-\frac{4}{9})=\frac{2}{3}-\frac{4}{9}.
$$

 

Now, we put the fractions over a common denominator of $9$ and combine the numerators, which gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3}-\frac{4}{9} & =\frac{6}{9}-\frac{4}{9}=\frac{6-4}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we work out $6-4$ using our number line.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14149424/assets/4ebf100b7da9bbada9145b4b5ea018cfee8ff2037307ca5023d6c2de54705fdd.png)

We find that $6-4=2.$ So, we get

$$
\frac{6-4}{9}=\frac{2}{9}.
$$
